summary.title: Computer Graphics from Scratch – Introduction
summary.one_liner: You learn what the book covers: building a software raytracer and a rasterizer for 3D scenes using only a PutPixel primitive, with no graphics APIs.
takeaways: The book builds two complete renderers, a raytracer and a rasterizer, that produce similar results on a simple scene.
The only primitive needed is a method to set a pixel's color; no OpenGL, Vulkan, Metal or DirectX is used.
Part I covers raytracing (spheres, lighting, shadows, reflections); Part II covers rasterization (lines, triangles, perspective, clipping, hidden surfaces, shading, textures).
Prerequisites are light: a little high-school trigonometry plus a linear algebra appendix; implementations are in JavaScript and run in a browser.
summary.summary: This is the introduction to an online book that teaches 3D rendering from first principles. It explains the book's audience (high-school students through professionals), its focus on simplicity, and its two-part structure: raytracing and rasterization, each built into a working renderer. It outlines the chapters in order, from canvas and colors through lighting, shadows, lines, triangles, perspective projection, clipping, textures, and an appendix on linear algebra. Pseudocode and links to JavaScript implementations are provided.
